heading: INT. HOSPITAL LAUNDRY ROOM, BASEMENT LEVEL - NIGHT

units.text: INT. HOSPITAL LAUNDRY ROOM, BASEMENT LEVEL - NIGHT
Steam, lint, the long sigh of industrial dryers.
Wire carts of folded scrubs stand in rows like pale choirs.
A radio on a shelf murmurs a ball game no one is following.
NURSE DOLORES FAIRWEATHER-NKEMELU (50s, reading glasses on a beaded chain) sits on an overturned bucket, a clipboard on her knees.
Across from her, DR. SAMANTHA VOSS-ITO (30s, exhausted, hair half out of its clip) leans against a warm machine with her eyes closed.
They have come down here to escape the ward for ten minutes, and neither has said so.
A third woman, LAUNDRY SUPERVISOR BERNADETTE QUILLON (60s, forearms like rope), folds a sheet with the metronomic calm of someone who has done it forty thousand times.
Near her, two younger orderlies stack towels: KESTUTIS BALODIS (20s, tall, a shy stammer) and ROSAURA MENDOZA-LIN (20s, a bright scarf around her hair).
Fourteen's stable. She asked for tea.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: She can have tea.
units.name: SAMANTHA

units.text: She wants it at four a.m.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: Then she wants it at four a.m.
units.name: SAMANTHA

units.text: Kettle's by the dryer. Help yourself.
units.name: BERNADETTE

units.text: You're an angel, Bernadette.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: I'm a woman with a kettle.
units.name: BERNADETTE

units.text: Samantha opens her eyes.
She watches Dolores pour water into a chipped mug, then hand it to Rosaura, who nods and slips away.
Dolores sits again; Bernadette snaps a sheet in the air and it floats down in a perfect rectangle.
Dr. Voss? M-may I ask?
units.name: KESTUTIS

units.text: Of course.
units.name: SAMANTHA

units.text: Does it g-get easier?
units.name: KESTUTIS

units.text: Samantha smiles, tired but kind.
Dolores glances at Bernadette.
Bernadette keeps folding.
The dryer ticks down.
Nobody answers him for a long moment.
It gets quieter.
units.name: SAMANTHA

units.text: Is that the same?
units.name: KESTUTIS

units.text: Not really, love.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: The radio announcer shouts about a home run.
Everyone lets it fill the silence.
